why: G1 names the same cause: the pattern supplied via -e/--regexp/-f or attached forms leaves the operand unspent so the file path is consumed as the pattern.
G2 identifies the same recursive-flag regex that cannot match --recursive/--dereference-recursive.
G8 identifies operandsAllowed=0 for sed/awk so their script operand is read as a path and piped filters are refused.
G4 identifies trigger tokens keeping stopwords/short words while query tokens drop them, so the every() order-free path never fires.
No finding flags that the per-command VALUE_FLAGS and the rg isFirst guard are unpinned by tests; G11 concerns a different module's test.
No finding covers word-boundary padding without stemming dropping inflected forms; G6 is about over-matching one-word triggers, the opposite problem.
